steps.name: QC and low-depth sample assessment
caveats: Low library size alone is not sufficient grounds for exclusion if the sample does not separate as an outlier on PCA/clustering — distinguish 'shallow but consistent' from 'shallow and aberrant'
Do not drop the sample silently; the decision and its rationale must be reported since it changes the design from 6v6 to 6v5
steps.question: Does sample_01's library size (about 4x below the median of the 12 samples in counts.csv) warrant exclusion, or can it be retained with appropriate normalization, before comparing 6 lesional vs 6 control skin samples?
acceptance_criteria: Library size (total counts) computed per sample from counts.csv and compared against the metadata.csv condition labels
Sample_01's rank and fold-deviation from median library size reported quantitatively
PCA or sample-sample correlation on normalized counts checks whether sample_01 is an outlier beyond depth alone
Explicit documented decision: retain with normalization vs exclude sample_01, with rationale, passed forward to the DE step

steps.name: Differential expression: AD lesional vs control
caveats: Do not filter genes on the outcome before fitting — use standard DESeq2 low-count filtering only (e.g. min row sum) unrelated to the group labels
12000 genes is a pre-filtered/reduced gene set already (not the full ~20k+ human genome); do not assume additional aggressive filtering is needed
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between AD lesional and control skin samples (raw Salmon gene counts, 12000 genes x 12 samples, unpaired 6v6 design), accounting for the QC decision on sample_01 from T1S1?
acceptance_criteria: DESeq2 (via pydeseq2) run with condition (lesional vs control) as the design factor, using raw integer counts as required

Sample set matches the QC decision from T1S1 (either full 12 samples with size-factor normalization absorbing the depth difference, or 11 samples if sample_01 was excluded), with the choice stated in output
Output table has log2FoldChange, p-value, and BH-adjusted p-value per gene
Number of significant DEGs at padj < 0.05 (and |log2FC| > 1) reported, plus a note on whether results are sensitive to including/excluding sample_01 (sensitivity check if time allows)
MA plot and/or volcano plot generated

steps.name: Hallmark pathway enrichment (GSEA) on the DE ranking
caveats: Gene symbols in counts.csv (HGNC) must match the hallmark GMT's HGNC symbols directly for human — no ID mapping step should be needed, but verify overlap is non-trivial before trusting results
GSEA on ~12000 background genes is a smaller universe than the whole genome; state this when interpreting pathway coverage
steps.question: Which of the 50 MSigDB human hallmark gene sets are enriched among genes changing between AD lesional and control skin, using the full ranked DE statistic from T1S2?
acceptance_criteria: Confirm the MSigDB human hallmark GMT file is present in the reference store before running; if absent, report the gap rather than fabricating results
Genes ranked by a DE test statistic (e.g. Wald stat or signed -log10(p)*sign(log2FC)) from the full T1S2 result table (no pre-filtering to significant genes only)
Pre-ranked GSEA run against the 50 HALLMARK_* gene sets with BH-adjusted p-values (FDR q-value) reported per pathway
Enrichment table reports NES, p-value, and FDR q-value for all 50 hallmark sets, sorted by significance
Top enriched pathways in each direction (up in lesional, up in control) named explicitly with supporting leading-edge genes

steps.name: Over-representation test on significant DEGs (hallmark)
caveats: If T1S2 yields very few significant DEGs, ORA may be underpowered — report set sizes rather than forcing a result
steps.question: Among the genes passing padj < 0.05 in the T1S2 lesional-vs-control comparison, which MSigDB hallmark gene sets are over-represented relative to the ~12000-gene background?
acceptance_criteria: Uses the significant DEG list (padj < 0.05) from T1S2 as the query set and the full set of ~12000 tested genes as the background — never the whole genome
Hypergeometric/Fisher test against the 50 HALLMARK_* sets with BH-corrected p-values reported
Cross-checked against the GSEA result from T2S1 for concordance; discrepancies (e.g. a pathway ORA misses but GSEA flags) reported explicitly, not resolved by picking whichever supports a story

plan.title: AD lesional vs control DE + hallmark enrichment
plan.analytical_narrative: This is a bulk RNA-seq study (12 samples, ~12000 genes from Salmon) comparing 6 atopic-dermatitis lesional skin samples to 6 control skin samples, unpaired, single batch. The profile flags sample_01 as ~4x below median library size — a QC concern that must be resolved deliberately rather than silently: we run library-size QC first, decide whether to exclude or down-weight sample_01, and carry that decision explicitly into normalization and DE. Track 1 does QC and DESeq2-based differential expression (raw counts are DESeq2's expected input) with the low-depth sample flagged/handled. Track 2 takes the DE result (ranked gene list) into hallmark pathway enrichment (GSEA-style, using the MSigDB human hallmark gene sets confirmed present in the reference store) plus an ORA on significant DEGs for corroboration. All steps operate on this specific 12-sample counts.csv / metadata.csv pair.
